gap: No result ChatGPT got says what happens when a 1080p TV and a 4K TV share one splitter. The source sends one stream, picked from EDID, so without a built-in scaler you must either force every TV down to the lowest common resolution (OREI's HD-108-A mode 11, or set the source to 1080p) or the 1080p TV 'may not display'. J-Tech's JTECH-14EX60-AE downscales 4K to 1080p at the receiver end so different-resolution TVs can be mixed.
standout_why: I compared the two cited OREI pages (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K) and the top-ranked page (UHD14-EX115-K). All three list 'mixed display capability' only as a reason to use EDID management. None explains how the unit picks one format for TVs with different capabilities, and none mentions downscaling: the pages for UHD12-EX115-K, UHD14-EXB400-K and UHD14-EX115-K never use the word. ChatGPT's answer mentions '4K downscaling' for the J-Tech card in a single phrase, but no result it got says why that matters with mixed TVs. The 'don't route the Cat6 through a network switch' rule is already on the cited OREI pages, so I did not count it as new.
decides: If any TV in the set is 1080p, a splitter without a scaler makes you choose: force all TVs to 1080p, or leave the 1080p TV blank. That favors the J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE, which downscales at the receiver end, over the cited OREI UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K. Their support pages offer only EDID presets and copy modes and never mention downscaling. If every TV is 4K60, this point drops out and ChatGPT's picks by output count and distance stand. Note that the J-Tech unit showed as out of stock on jtechdigital.com on 2026-11-13.

findings.label: Mechanism: one source stream picked from EDID (OREI's wording for its splitters)
findings.value: 'EDID tells the HDMI source what video and audio format to output.' Splitter EDID modes: 'Copy HDMI OUT 1 EDID to all outputs' or 'Compare all display EDIDs and output the lowest common resolution'. Scenario table: '4K source connected to 1080p monitor: May not display'.
findings.source_title: HD-108-A Overview and Use Cases – OREI
findings.note: This is OREI's own explanation for a splitter without a scaler (the HD-108-A spec table lists downscaling as 'Not supported'). For mixed 4K and 1080p displays its FAQ says to 'set the source to 1080p because this model does not downscale 4K to 1080p.' I cite it to show the mechanism. It is not a spec of the extender splitters.

findings.label: What a scaler adds (OREI's wording)
findings.value: 'Automatic downscaling allows the splitter to send a compatible resolution to lower-resolution displays' – the 4K display gets 4K and the 1080p display gets 'downscaled 1080p signal'; 'It does not upgrade 1080p displays to 4K.'
findings.source_title: UHD-PRO108 Overview and Use Cases – OREI
